title: Stable influence as a noisy norm
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $P$ be a finite product probability space with $n$ coordinates, and let $\rho\ge 0$. For every real-valued function $f$ on its outcome space and every coordinate $i$, $\rho I_i^{(\rho)}(f)=\|T_{\sqrt{\rho}}L_i f\|_{2,P}^{2}$.
hypotheses_covered: $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and a finite product probability space $P$ with $n$ coordinates
A real-valued function $f$ on the outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $\rho\ge0$, a coordinate $i$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\rho I_i^{(\rho)}(f)=\|T_{\sqrt\rho}L_if\|_{2,P}^2$, where $I_i^{(\rho)}$ is stable influence and $L_i$ is the coordinate Laplacian. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $L_i h=h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h$; $I_i^{(a)}(h)=\sum_{S\ni i}a^{|S|-1}\mathbb E_Ph_S^2$ for $a\in\mathbb R$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
